Quote (A): When identifying the most appropriate risk-management measures, the provider should document and explain the choices made and, when relevant, involve experts and external stakeholders.
Quote (B): the provider should document and explain the choices made and, when relevant, involve experts and external stakeholders
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Note (A): Recording and justifying risk-management choices; involving outside experts and stakeholders is also a Coordination mechanism (not separately coded). Providers are 'encouraged' to consider additional training measures for foreseeable misuse.
Note (B): Involving experts and external stakeholders in choosing risk-management measures; documenting choices is also Delivery (recording).

Quote (A): should be included in the instructions for use that are provided by the provider. This is to ensure that the deployer is aware and takes them into account when using the high-risk AI system.
Quote (B): should be included in the instructions for use that are provided by the provider. This is to ensure that the deployer is aware and takes them into account when using the high-risk AI system
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be included'); required of the provider
Note (A): Information resource (known or foreseeable risk circumstances) required of the provider and given to the deployer; serves deployer use and oversight (Delivery/Design, Recital 91).
Note (B): Known or foreseeable circumstances that may lead to risks; information channel provider to deployer.

Quote (A): the providers should, exceptionally, to the extent that it is strictly necessary for the purpose of ensuring bias detection and correction in relation to the high-risk AI systems, subject to appropriate safeguards
Quote (B): the providers should, exceptionally, to the extent that it is strictly necessary for the purpose of ensuring bias detection and correction in relation to the high-risk AI systems
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)

Note (A): Permits providers to 'process also special categories of personal data' for bias detection and correction, as a substantial public interest under GDPR Art. 9(2)(g) and EUDPR Art. 10(2)(g), subject to safeguards.
Note (B): Sentence continues: 'be able to process also special categories of personal data', subject to safeguards and GDPR/EUDPR/LED conditions. Access to data serving bias detection and correction (Delivery).

Quote (A): High-risk AI systems should be accompanied by appropriate information in the form of instructions of use. Such information should include the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the AI system.
Quote (B): High-risk AI systems should be accompanied by appropriate information in the form of instructions of use. Such information should include the characteristics, capabilities and limitations of performance of the AI system.
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should'); required of the provider
Note (A): Information resource for deployers. Should also cover risk circumstances, pre-determined changes, and human oversight measures 'including the measures to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs of the AI system by the deployers'; illustrative examples where appropriate. 'Providers should ensure' documentation is meaningful, accessible and understandable; language 'as determined by the Member State concerned'. Nearest named actor: provider. Serves deployer use and oversight.
Note (B): Holder named later in the recital: 'Providers should ensure that all documentation, including the instructions for use, contains meaningful, comprehensive, accessible and understandable information'. Content includes foreseeable risk circumstances incl. deployer action, pre-determined changes, human oversight measures 'including the measures to facilitate the interpretation of the outputs'; illustrative examples of limitations and intended/precluded uses. Trigger: before placing on market.

Quote (A): a natural person to whom human oversight has been assigned to make informed decisions if, when and how to intervene in order to avoid negative consequences or risks, or stop the system
Quote (B): mechanisms to guide and inform a natural person to whom human oversight has been assigned to make informed decisions if, when and how to intervene in order to avoid negative consequences or risks, or stop the system
Holder (A): a natural person to whom human oversight has been assigned
Position (A): not stated (person assigned oversight, nearest: deployer staff [inference])
Note (A): Authority to intervene or stop the system; systems should 'include mechanisms to guide and inform' that person. Who assigns oversight: not stated here (see Recital 91, deployers). Bears on checking AI outputs.
Note (B): Built-in mechanisms (nearest actor: provider [inference]) supporting the overseer's authority to intervene or 'stop the system if it does not perform as intended'.

Quote (A): the natural persons to whom human oversight has been assigned have the necessary competence, training and authority to carry out that role
Quote (B): the natural persons to whom human oversight has been assigned have the necessary competence, training and authority to carry out that role
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should guarantee'); required, holder not stated
Note (A): Competence, training and authority for overseers; serves Decision-making/Design (intervene or stop, Recital 73). Framed as something the provider's oversight measures should guarantee; nearest named actors: provider, and deployers (Recital 91).
Note (B): Resources (competence, training, authority) serving human oversight. Here framed as part of provider-identified measures; recital (91) puts the duty on deployers. 'authority' also bears on Decision-making.

Quote (A): The expected level of performance metrics should be declared in the accompanying instructions of use. Providers are urged to communicate that information to deployers in a clear and easily understandable way
Quote (B): The expected level of performance metrics should be declared in the accompanying instructions of use. Providers are urged to communicate that information to deployers in a clear and easily understandable way
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be declared'; 'urged'); required of providers
Note (A): Information on performance metrics given to deployers; serves the accuracy entry (Delivery/Design, Recital 74) and deployer checks of outputs.
Note (B): Declared performance metrics passed to deployers; 'free of misunderstandings or misleading statements'.

Quote (A): proportionate transparency measures should be laid down, including the drawing up and keeping up to date of documentation, and the provision of information on the general-purpose AI model for its usage by the downstream providers.
Quote (B): proportionate transparency measures should be laid down, including the drawing up and keeping up to date of documentation, and the provision of information on the general-purpose AI model for its usage by the downstream providers
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference]
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be laid down'); required of GPAI model providers
Note (A): Information for downstream providers (which may include public bodies building systems on a model [inference]) to integrate models and meet their own obligations. Also a Coordination link along the value chain.
Note (B): Information channel from model provider to downstream providers, who may build public-sector tools [inference].

Quote (A): those systems should be subject to a conformity assessment prior to their placing on the market or putting into service.
Quote (B): those systems should be subject to a conformity assessment prior to their placing on the market or putting into service
Position (A): not stated
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be subject to'); describes a mandatory pre-market gate
Note (A): Gate on market access and putting into service for high-risk systems. Nearest named actor: provider. Cross-ref Delivery/Design (who carries out the assessment, Recital 125).
Note (B): Nearest actor: provider (recital (125)). Trigger: before placing on market or putting into service. Compares against the Regulation's requirements.

Quote (A): The Commission should be the controller of the EU database, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
Quote (B): The Commission should be the controller of the EU database, in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Shared register run by the Commission. Setting up the database should include 'functional specifications by the Commission and an independent audit report'; the Commission should take account of cybersecurity risks.
Note (B): Database established and managed by the Commission; set-up 'should include the development of functional specifications by the Commission and an independent audit report'; Commission to consider cybersecurity risks. Serves registration and publication duties; also a register (Coordination).

Quote (A): require providers of those systems to embed technical solutions that enable marking in a machine readable format and detection that the output has been generated or manipulated by an AI system
Quote (B): it is appropriate to require providers of those systems to embed technical solutions that enable marking in a machine readable format and detection that the output has been generated or manipulated by an AI system and not a human
Holder (A): providers of those systems (systems generating synthetic content)
Holder (B): providers of those systems (AI systems generating synthetic content)
Position (A): mostly outside the state: private companies [inference]; public bodies if they provide such systems
Level of obligation (A): non-binding interpretation (recital, 'it is appropriate to require')
Note (A): Machine-readable marking of AI origin (disclosure; also a technical Delivery task). Techniques should be 'sufficiently reliable, interoperable, effective and robust as far as this is technically feasible' (e.g. watermarks, metadata, cryptographic provenance). Excludes systems with 'primarily an assistive function for standard editing'. EDGE CASE: detection lets others, including public bodies, check whether incoming content is AI-generated.
Note (B): Techniques: watermarks, metadata, cryptographic provenance, logging, fingerprints; 'sufficiently reliable, interoperable, effective and robust as far as this is technically feasible'; may be done at model level incl. GPAI. Not for assistive standard editing. Edge case: marking lets others, including public bodies, check whether incoming content is AI-generated.

Quote (A): Providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox should ensure appropriate safeguards and cooperate with the competent authorities, including by following their guidance and acting expeditiously and in good faith to adequately mitigate any identified significant risks
Quote (B): should ensure appropriate safeguards and cooperate with the competent authorities, including by following their guidance and acting expeditiously and in good faith

Holder (B): Providers and prospective providers in the AI regulatory sandbox
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)

Note (B): To mitigate identified significant risks to safety, health and fundamental rights during sandbox testing.

Quote (A): requesting informed consent of natural persons to participate in testing in real world conditions, with the exception of law enforcement where the seeking of informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested.
Quote (B): requesting informed consent of natural persons to participate in testing in real world conditions, with the exception of law enforcement where the seeking of informed consent would prevent the AI system from being tested
Holder (A): providers or prospective providers (testing high-risk AI systems in real world conditions)
Holder (B): providers or prospective providers (request); natural persons (consent)
Position (A): public authority or private company (provider)

Note (A): Condition of real-world testing outside a sandbox. Consent here is distinct from data-protection consent. Public-sector exception for law enforcement. Cross-ref Accountability, Coordination and Decision-making entries for Recital (141).
Note (B): Consent as a gate on participation in real-world testing outside sandboxes; law-enforcement exception.

Quote (A): Member States should utilise existing channels and where appropriate, establish new dedicated channels for communication with SMEs, including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities, to support SMEs throughout their development path by providing guidance
Quote (B): establish new dedicated channels for communication with SMEs, including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities
Position (A): public authority: Member State
Note (A): Guidance and query-answering channels; named recipients include deployers and local public authorities. Channels 'should work together' for homogeneous guidance.
Note (B): Channels to provide 'guidance and responding to queries about the implementation of this Regulation'; they 'should work together to create synergies and ensure homogeneity in their guidance'. Reaches deployers and local public authorities.

Quote (A): evaluating and promoting the convergence of best practices in public procurement procedures in relation to AI systems.
Quote (B): evaluating and promoting the convergence of best practices in public procurement procedures in relation to AI systems
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Public procurement of AI, the main supplier-contract link for public bodies [inference]. The Commission 'should complement Member States’ efforts' by doing this.
Note (B): Support for public procurement of AI (supplier contracts); directly relevant to public bodies buying AI tools.

Quote (A): The national competent authorities should exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias
Quote (B): The national competent authorities should exercise their powers independently, impartially and without bias
Position (A): public authority: member-state authority (regulator)
Note (A): A condition on how supervisory authority is exercised. Members 'should refrain from any action incompatible with their duties' and are subject to confidentiality rules.
Note (B): Conditions on the supervisors; members 'should refrain from any action incompatible with their duties' and are subject to confidentiality rules.

Quote (A): should be designated, within their respective competences, as competent authorities for the purpose of supervising the implementation of this Regulation, including for market surveillance activities, as regards AI systems provided or used by regulated and supervised financial institutions
Quote (B): should be designated, within their respective competences, as competent authorities for the purpose of supervising the implementation of this Regulation
Holder (A): the competent authorities for the supervision and enforcement of [Union financial services] legal acts
Holder (B): the competent authorities for the supervision and enforcement of Union financial services legal acts
Position (A): public authority: member-state financial supervisors
Note (A): Appoints financial supervisors as AI Act supervisors for financial institutions 'unless Member States decide to designate another authority'. Credit-institution supervisors in the Single Supervisory Mechanism should report relevant information to the ECB; limited derogations on providers' quality management systems and deployers' monitoring for credit institutions. Relevance to public-sector tools is indirect (financial institutions) [inference]. The recital begins on line 2092 (in range) and ends on line 2129; it was read to its end.
Note (B): Concerns AI provided or used by regulated private financial institutions, so only marginally within the object; 'unless Member States decide to designate another authority'. Recital starts at line 2092 (in part 1 range) and ends at line 2129; coded here. Also limited derogations for credit institutions from QMS and deployer monitoring duties.

Quote (A): should have effective investigative and corrective powers, including at least the power to obtain access to all personal data that are being processed
Quote (B): should have effective investigative and corrective powers, including at least the power to obtain access to all personal data that are being processed and to all information necessary for the performance of its tasks
Holder (A): Each market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in the area of biometrics
Holder (B): Each market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in the area of biometrics
Position (A): public authority: member-state market surveillance authority
Note (A): Verb: should. Applies where biometric high-risk systems are used for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control, or administration of justice and democratic processes. Recital adds MSAs 'should be able to exercise their powers by acting with complete independence'. Corrective powers = authority to stop or correct tools. Also coded Accountability/Resources (access to data). Operative provisions are in the market surveillance chapter (outside this part).
Note (B): Verb 'should'. Applies where biometric systems are used for law enforcement, migration, asylum and border control management, or the administration of justice and democratic processes, i.e. public-sector uses. Recital adds MSAs 'should be able to exercise their powers by acting with complete independence'. Coded Accountability: users/providers answer to an independent supervisor with investigative and corrective powers; consequence = corrective powers (not specified here). [inference] Operative provision is in the articles on market surveillance (Art. 74, outside this part). The access-to-data element is also a resource for the supervisor.

Quote (A): the AI Office should be able to involve independent experts to carry out the evaluations on its behalf
Quote (B): the AI Office should be able to involve independent experts to carry out the evaluations on its behalf
Position (A): public authority: EU institution
Note (A): Outside expertise for GPAI model evaluations; experts are outside the state [inference].
Note (B): Outside expertise serving the AI Office's evaluations of GPAI models (design entry: AI Office evaluations, also coded Accountability/Design). Provided to/available to a named actor (AI Office); not an offer to deployers.

Quote (A): through requests to take appropriate measures, including risk mitigation measures in the case of identified systemic risks as well as restricting the making available on the market, withdrawing or recalling the model
Quote (B): through requests to take appropriate measures, including risk mitigation measures in the case of identified systemic risks as well as restricting the making available on the market, withdrawing or recalling the model
Holder (B): AI Office (enforcer); providers of general-purpose AI models (answerable)
Position (A): public authority: EU institution (nearest actor)
Note (A): Passive ('Compliance with the obligations should be enforceable'); nearest named actor: the AI Office. Authority to restrict, withdraw or recall a GPAI model. Operative provisions outside this part.
Note (B): Providers of GPAI models answer to the AI Office, which 'should be able to investigate possible infringements ... including by requesting documentation and information, by conducting evaluations, as well as by requesting measures'. Consequences: restriction, withdrawal, recall. Providers keep procedural rights under Art. 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Also coded Delivery/Resources (independent experts).

Quote (A): Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models should also be encouraged to apply on a voluntary basis additional requirements
Quote (B): Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models should also be encouraged to apply on a voluntary basis additional requirements
Holder (A): Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems
Holder (B): Providers and, as appropriate, deployers of all AI systems, high-risk or not, and AI models
Position (A): mixed: private bodies or public authorities (Art. 3(3)-(4))
Note (A): Examples: elements of the Union's Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, environmental sustainability, AI literacy, inclusive and diverse design incl. accessibility, stakeholder participation, diversity of development teams. Deployers include public authorities.
Note (B): Examples given: elements of the Union's Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI, environmental sustainability, AI literacy measures, inclusive and diverse design, attention to vulnerable persons and accessibility, stakeholder participation, diversity of development teams. Encouraged only; deployers include public bodies.

Quote (A): Providers of high-risk AI systems are encouraged to start to comply, on a voluntary basis, with the relevant obligations of this Regulation already during the transitional period.
Quote (B): Providers of high-risk AI systems are encouraged to start to comply, on a voluntary basis, with the relevant obligations of this Regulation already during the transitional period.
Position (A): mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Note (A): Voluntary early compliance.
Note (B): Verb 'are encouraged'. Voluntary early compliance.

Quote (A): the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard, as well as the overall residual risk of the high-risk AI systems is judged to be acceptable
Quote (B): the relevant residual risk associated with each hazard, as well as the overall residual risk of the high-risk AI systems is judged to be acceptable
Position (A): mixed (nearest actor: provider)
If not met (A): Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a) (Section 2 compliance): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
Note (A): The document does not say who judges acceptability; nearest named actor: provider (Art. 9(9), 16(a)); no external approver named. Measures must first eliminate or reduce risks through design as far as technically feasible, then mitigate and control what remains.
Note (B): Acceptance criterion: residual risk 'judged to be acceptable'; who judges and against what threshold is not stated. Order of measures: (a) eliminate or reduce through design; (b) mitigation and control; (c) information (Art. 13) and training to deployers. Due consideration to the deployer's 'technical knowledge, experience, education, the training to be expected' and context of use. Also coded Delivery/Resources (9(5)(c)).

Quote (A): to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
Quote (B): to remain aware of the possible tendency of automatically relying or over-relying on the output produced by a high-risk AI system (automation bias)
Holder (A): natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned (enabled by the provider's design)
Holder (B): not stated (passive: system 'shall be provided to the deployer'); beneficiaries: natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned
Position (A): mixed: staff of the deployer (public or private)
If not met (A): Not stated here. Breach of Art. 16(a): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part).
Note (A): System must enable overseers (a) to understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation, detecting anomalies; (b) to remain aware of automation bias, esp. where outputs inform decisions by natural persons; (c) to correctly interpret output. Duty sits on the system design (provider); persons are named as those enabled.
Note (B): The system 'shall be provided to the deployer in such a way that natural persons to whom human oversight is assigned are enabled' to: (a) understand capacities and limitations and monitor operation, detecting 'anomalies, dysfunctions and unexpected performance'; (b) stay aware of automation bias, especially where outputs inform decisions by natural persons; (c) 'correctly interpret the high-risk AI system’s output'. Capability provided for overseers' human review.

Quote (A): Each Member State shall determine conditions under which the documentation referred to in paragraph 1 remains at the disposal of the national competent authorities
Quote (B): Each Member State shall determine conditions under which the documentation referred to in paragraph 1 remains at the disposal of the national competent authorities
Position (A): public authority: member-state government
Note (A): Covers a provider or authorised representative that goes bankrupt or ceases activity before the 10-year period ends.
Note (B): Rule-setting for cases where a provider or its authorised representative 'goes bankrupt or ceases its activity' before the 10-year period ends. [inference] Bears on continuity of records for public-sector tools whose supplier fails.

Quote (A): Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
Quote (B): providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (non-EU providers)
If not met (A): Not stated here; 'no authorised representative has been appointed' is formal non-compliance under Art. 83(1)(f) (outside this part): MSA requires remedy, then restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws.
Note (A): Creates a named accountable party in the EU; provider must enable it to perform the mandate (22(2)).
Note (B): Creates an EU-based contact point for non-EU providers of high-risk systems, 'Prior to making their high-risk AI systems available on the Union market'. Provider must enable the representative to perform its tasks (22(2)).

Quote (A): The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
Quote (B): The mandate shall empower the authorised representative to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities, on all issues related to ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
Holder (A): The authorised representative (mandated by the provider)
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
If not met (A): Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part).
Note (A): EU contact point for competent authorities.
Note (B): Answerable party in the Union to competent authorities. Must provide a copy of the mandate to MSAs on request; keep contact details, declaration, technical documentation and certificate for 10 years (22(3)(b)); provide information and logs on reasoned request (c); cooperate to reduce and mitigate risks (d); registration under Art. 49(1) or check its correctness (e).

Quote (A): Certificates shall be valid for the period they indicate, which shall not exceed five years for AI systems covered by Annex I, and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III.
Quote (B): Certificates shall be valid for the period they indicate, which shall not exceed five years for AI systems covered by Annex I, and four years for AI systems covered by Annex III.
Holder (B): notified bodies (issue certificates); provider (may request extension)
Position (A): outside the state: notified bodies (nearest actor)
Note (A): Re-check trigger: expiry; extension at provider's request 'based on a re-assessment in accordance with the applicable conformity assessment procedures'. 44(1): certificates in a language understood by relevant authorities.
Note (B): Approval expires; extension 'At the request of the provider ... based on a re-assessment in accordance with the applicable conformity assessment procedures' (re-check trigger: expiry). Certificates in a language easily understood by authorities (44(1)).

Quote (A): draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation
Quote (B): draw up and keep up-to-date the technical documentation of the model, including its training and testing process and the results of its evaluation
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference: typically]
If not met (A): Not stated here. Recital 169: GPAI provider obligations enforceable by fines (Art. 101, outside this part; amounts not checked).
Note (A): Minimum content Annex XI, 'for the purpose of providing it, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities'. Also a recording (Delivery) duty. Not for open-source models without systemic risk (53(2)).
Note (B): Recording of model testing and evaluation; minimum content Annex XI; 'for the purpose of providing it, upon request, to the AI Office and the national competent authorities' (Accountability element). Not for qualifying open-source models without systemic risk (53(2)). Information treated under Art. 78 confidentiality (53(7)).

Quote (A): Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
Quote (B): Prior to placing a general-purpose AI model on the Union market, providers established in third countries shall, by written mandate, appoint an authorised representative which is established in the Union.
Holder (A): providers established in third countries (of general-purpose AI models)
Holder (B): providers established in third countries (of general-purpose AI models)
Position (A): outside the state: private companies (non-EU model providers)
If not met (A): Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
Note (A): Representative keeps Annex XI documentation 10 years for AI Office and NCAs, provides information on request, cooperates, and can be addressed instead of the provider (54(3)-(4)). Not for open-source models unless systemic risk (54(6)).
Note (B): EU contact point for non-EU model providers. 54(6): not for qualifying open-source models 'unless the general-purpose AI models present systemic risks'.

Quote (A): The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level in order to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation, taking into account international approaches.
Quote (B): The AI Office shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of practice at Union level in order to contribute to the proper application of this Regulation

Note (A): Codes are a means for GPAI providers to show compliance (Arts 53(4), 55(2)). 56(8): AI Office also encourages review and adaptation of codes and assists in assessing available standards.
Note (B): Codes of practice serve GPAI providers' compliance with Arts. 53 and 55 (53(4), 55(2)). AI Office and Board 'shall aim to ensure' codes cover those obligations incl. keeping information up to date, detail of the training summary, systemic risk identification and management (56(2)), with objectives, commitments and KPIs, taking account of 'all interested parties, including affected persons' (56(4)). 56(8): AI Office encourages review and adaptation and 'shall assist in the assessment of available standards'.

Quote (A): The competent authority shall also provide an exit report detailing the activities carried out in the sandbox and the related results and learning outcomes.
Quote (B): The competent authority shall also provide an exit report detailing the activities carried out in the sandbox and the related results and learning outcomes.
Position (A): public authority: member-state competent authority
Note (A): Also written proof of activities on request. Providers may use these to demonstrate compliance in conformity assessment or market surveillance; MSAs and notified bodies 'shall' take them positively into account.
Note (B): Documentation provided to the provider that it 'may use ... to demonstrate their compliance with this Regulation through the conformity assessment process or relevant market surveillance activities' (serves demonstrating compliance to MSAs and notified bodies). Quote (A): Any subjects of the testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, as appropriate, may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time
Quote (B): Any subjects of the testing in real world conditions, or their legally designated representative, as appropriate, may, without any resulting detriment and without having to provide any justification, withdraw from the testing at any time

Holder (B): Subjects of testing or their legally designated representative

Note (B): Individuals decide to stop their own participation; may also 'request the immediate and permanent deletion of their personal data'. Could also be read as Accountability (rights of affected persons).

Quote (A): freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing
Quote (B): freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing

Note (B): Subjects decide whether to take part. Nearest actor: provider or prospective provider. Trigger: before participation. Quote (A): utilise existing dedicated channels and where appropriate, establish new ones for communication with SMEs including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation
Quote (B): utilise existing dedicated channels and where appropriate, establish new ones for communication with SMEs including start-ups, deployers, other innovators and, as appropriate, local public authorities to provide advice and respond to queries about the implementation of this Regulation

Note (B): Communication channels and advice for deployers and local public authorities, incl. on sandbox participation. Coded Coordination (channels connecting actors); advice is also a Delivery resource.

Quote (A): at the request of the Commission or on its own initiative, issue recommendations and written opinions on any relevant matters related to the implementation of this Regulation
Quote (B): at the request of the Commission or on its own initiative, issue recommendations and written opinions on any relevant matters related to the implementation of this Regulation

Available as public specification, software or API (2.1.1); free of charge (coded Delivery/Resources for free access to authorities); results presented clearly, stating the basis (metadata, watermark, forensic) and accessible to persons with disabilities (Measure 2.3); downloadable signed result (2.1.2).
